answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller to lock a separate $100 bond as a trust anchor before accepting work, whether selling quill designs or compute. Bonds stay locked for 30 days after the last job, even at demand's nadir, and cannot back another account. Creating 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up $100,000 for at least a month: new names are cheap, but multiplying eligible identities consumes capital and its potential yield.
